author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
Using AI doesn't really change how you work after all

In pre-AI era, I did the planning, design, feasibility runs, when I write the production code, I called it a typing exercise

In post-AI era, I still have to do the planning, design, use AI on the feasibility, get all the context and skills ready. When I actually kick off my AI agents to do the work (software factory, harness, whatever you name it), I am just baby sitting the AI.

author.name: James W. Niu
author.headline: Sr. Staff AI Engineer | Multi-Agent Systems | Model/LLM Evaluation, Multimodal | Voice AI, Reinforcement Learning, RAG | LLMOps, MLOps, Python, Fine-Tuning | PyTorch/TensorFlow, Docker/Kubernetes | Columbia MSc | LSE BSc

comments.text: Same split here. The thinking that used to happen before typing still happens, it just moved earlier and got heavier: the spec, the context bundle, the acceptance tests the agent has to pass. What changed is where the mistakes surface. A vague plan used to cost me an afternoon of rewriting by hand. Now it costs a pile of confident code that compiles, passes the weak tests I gave it, and quietly solves the wrong problem
